rejected.title: Quality of evidence
card: Valid
Evidence is valid when the investigation measures what it claims to measure and fairly tests the question. A fair test changes one variable, keeps the others controlled and uses suitable methods.
Authoritative
An authoritative source is written by people with expertise in the area. Their work is usually reviewed by other experts and names its methods and data.
Errors
Random errors make repeated measurements scatter. Systematic errors push results the same way each time, such as a balance that reads too high. Both lower the quality of evidence.
Bias
Bias is when interests or expectations shape how an investigation is done or reported. Checking who paid for the work and what was left out helps spot it.
rejected.remember: Good evidence tests the right thing, comes from experts, and has its errors and bias checked.

a.q: Ravi wants to test whether a fertiliser makes bean plants grow taller. He gives the fertiliser to plants on a sunny windowsill and gives none to plants in a dark cupboard. Why is his evidence weak?
opts: It is not valid, because light also differs between groups
It is biased, because the fertiliser was made by a company
It has random error, because the plants were measured twice
It is not authoritative, because Ravi is a school student
a.why: A fair test changes only one variable. Here light differs as well as fertiliser, so the investigation does not fairly test the question and the evidence is not valid. Being a student does not make results weak if the method is sound.
a.clue: How many things differ between the two groups of plants?

b.q: A drink company pays a laboratory to test its bottled water. The report says the water is the purest available, but it does not give the methods or the data. Which concern about this evidence is the most direct?
opts: Bias, because the company paid and left out its data
Random error, because the samples came from one factory
Systematic error, because the company paid for the test
Not valid, because the water was tested in a laboratory
b.why: The company paid for the report and has an interest in the result, and leaving out the methods and data stops others checking it. These are the signs of bias. Systematic error comes from the measuring, such as a faulty balance, not from who paid for the work.
b.clue: Who paid for the work, and what was left out of the report?

b.q: A drink company pays a laboratory to test its bottled water. The report says the water is the purest available, but it does not give the methods or the data. Which concern about this evidence is the most direct?
opts: Possible bias, and the methods are not shown for checking
Random error, because the water was tested in a laboratory
Systematic error, because the company sells bottled water
It is invalid, because laboratories cannot test water purity
